 ‘Get (Kirk) Herbstreit Off My TV,’ ‘Trying So Hard to Fake Interest’ — NFL Fans Rip Veteran Broadcaster’s ‘Irritating’ Commentary on Jaguars-Ravens
 Fans took aim at Kirk Herbstreit's "terrible" commentary during the Jaguars' 33-10 win over Ravens, from his pronunciation to his fit beside Al Michaels.
 November 6, 2026 | 2:12 AM EST 
 Thursday night turned into a long one for more than just the Baltimore Ravens. The Jacksonville Jaguars rolled to a 33-10 win at M&T Bank Stadium, holding undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano to 10-of-18 passing for 60 yards with two interceptions in his first NFL start.
 But as the game dragged on, fans took aim at Prime Video analyst Kirk Herbstreit for several reasons. One fan even wanted Herbstreit off the broadcast altogether, while several others took issue with his “fake interest” in a game that was lopsided from the jump.
 Dive into PFSN’s NFL Mock Draft Simulator and run a mock by yourself or with your friends! 
 NFL Fans Call Out Kirk Herbstreit’s “Irritating” Commentary on TNF
 Herbstreit called the game as the analyst beside Al Michaels. The Ravens came in on a three-game losing streak and turned to Fagnano after losing Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley to injuries in Buffalo.
 As the night wore on, one fan minced no words about the quality of the broadcast. “Get Herbstreit off my TV,” the viewer wrote, referring to Herbstreit’s comments on Fagnano’s wife, Lydia, when he said, “His wife may have a postgame breakdown in the kitchen.”
 “His wife may have a post game breakdown in the kitchen” get Herbstreit off my tv
 — Ashlie (@EMT_Ashlie) November 6, 2026 
 Earlier, Herbstreit also noted that Lydia had been helping Joe prepare by running walkthroughs in their living room and reading plays to him.
 Meanwhile, another complaint came down to the basics of commentary. “Kirk Herbstreit is getting paid $20 million a year to call football games, but he can’t pronounce the word ‘Jaguars’ correctly. So irritating,” a fan wrote.
 Kirk Herbstreit is getting paid $20 million a year to call football games, but he can’t pronounce the word “Jaguars” correctly. So irritating.
 — Kenny BooYah! 🖖🏾 (@KwikWarren) November 6, 2026 
 SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer 
 The criticism went beyond delivery to the booth pairing itself. “I’ll state once again: Kirk Herbstreit is stealing money from Amazon; he adds nothing to the TNF NFL broadcast,” a fan wrote.
 I’ll state once again: Kirk Herbstreit is stealing money from Amazon, he adds nothing to the TNF NFL broadcast – if they would wake up and get a new broadcast partner for Al Michaels, the energy level and quality would go up so much (and the viewers) – Al still has it in him and is one of the best of all time
 — MobyWhaler (@rufusjonz) November 6, 2026 
 How Herbstreit came across beside Michaels caught another fan’s eye as well: “Kirk Herbstreit looks like he’s trying so hard to fake interest in whatever Al Michaels is talking about right now.”
 Kirk Herbstreit looks like he’s trying so hard to fake interest in whatever Al Michaels is talking about right now.
 — Nelson (@BelgerNelson) November 6, 2026 
 Michaels did not escape criticism entirely, though, as another fan went after both men and the state of the game: “I will be staying up until 11:30 ET to hate watch the Ravens in a blowout, with Al Michaels talking about who knows what and Kirk Herbstreit providing derisive, uninformed, passive-aggressive comments about analytics.”
 Yes I will be staying up until 11:30ET to hate watch the Ravens in a blowout, with Al Michaels talking about who knows what and Kirk Herbstreit providing derisive, uninformed, passive-aggressive comments about analytics
 — Jeremy Betz (@thebetz93) November 6, 2026 
 PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor 
 Coming back to the game, after Jake Moody’s 53-yard field goal pulled the Ravens within 7-3 in the first quarter, the Jaguars scored the next 26 points, 12 of them on Cam Little field goals, and all three of Baltimore’s turnovers came after halftime.
 Fagnano finished with a 22.7 passer rating as Baltimore managed 55 net passing yards, while Trevor Lawrence threw for 242 yards and a touchdown without an interception. The Ravens’ lone touchdown came on Justice Hill’s 65-yard run with Baltimore already trailing 33-3.
